one_month_reasoning: Events in the window: (1) Intuitive Q3 2026 results on Oct 20 after the close (consensus non-GAAP EPS ~$2.54-2.64), where management will quantify the 2027 Extended Use Program and frame 2027. Q3 2025 procedures grew ~19%, a tough comp, and the customer side points to Q3 U.S. growth at or slightly below Q2's 12%: HCA's 10-Q shows same-facility uninsured admissions +23.4%, exchange admissions -15% and same-facility outpatient surgeries -3.4%, its CFO reaffirmed the elective slowdown on Sept 15, and an Evercore ISI survey (Sept 23) found 24% of hospital execs already seeing slower procedures. (2) HCA/Tenet/UHS Q3 prints in late October give a second read on elective deferral. (3) Rates: the Fed hiked on Sept 16 and the 10-year reached ~5.2% in late September, a headwind for long-duration medtech multiples that is already partly priced. A Hugo general-surgery clearance is possible but Medtronic has given no dated timeline, so I treat it as headline risk rather than a window event (correcting round 1). Offsetting: OUS (~19%) and da Vinci 5 trade-ins should keep placements firm, the stock already trades ~33x 2027 EPS after a ~30% YTD fall, and an EUP number inside the 1-3% I&A/procedure range would be roughly what is priced. Net: two-sided, no edge; I use a lognormal with median ~$400.5 (a hair below spot for the tough comp and rate backdrop) and an 11.5% sigma (above the 37%/3.5 = 10.6% baseline for the earnings event).

fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (FY2028 non-GAAP EPS est. $13.45 x 32x = $430, less ~$4/share expected litigation cost = $426, weight 0.6) and FCF yield (FY2028 FCF/share est. $13.24 / 3.1% = $427, less $4 = $423, weight 0.4), valued as of Oct 2027; FY2027 EPS haircut ~3% to consensus for EUP (1-3% I&A/procedure range), ACA/Medicaid deferral and China.

inputs_detail.derivation: Aggregator consensus; one underlying source, not independent confirmations.

Consensus midpoint ~$12.20 less ~3%: EUP 2.0 launches H1 2027 on cost-sensitive procedures; I now use a 1-3% 2027 I&A/procedure drag (midpoint 2%) instead of leaning on the single-source 2020 '-2% actual' outcome; with I&A ~60% of revenue and half-year phase-in, net of some volume elasticity, ~1.3% EPS; third-party remanufacturing (Restore Robotics clearances, permitted under Intuitive contracts) adds modest I&A pricing pressure in the same benign procedures. ACA/coverage deferral ~1.5% (raised from ~1%): HCA 10-Q shows uninsured admissions +23.4%, not the +15% I used, and Medicaid work requirements start 2027-01-01. China tender share 62%->37% with ASP -19% ~0.3%.

2026 procedure growth guide 13.5-15.5% decelerating to ~12% in 2027-28 with modest operating leverage (Q2 non-GAAP op margin 42.1%, opex growth guide 11-13%) plus ~1%/yr buyback accretion; trimmed from 14% for a slower ACA lap.

Stock at ~33x consensus FY2027 EPS. Cut from 33x by one turn because the Fed hiked on 2026-09-16 and the 10-year moved above 5% (~5.2% by late September), the highest since 2007, which compresses multiples on long-duration growth. I do not go to 31x because the industry evidence still says competitors are sub-scale through 2027 (Ottava limited launch; Hugo general-surgery 510(k)s pending with no date; ~250 Hugo units targeted globally vs 11,710 da Vinci). Sell-side average PT ~$476 (~37x 2027) is evidence that 32x is not aggressive.

Ninth Circuit reversed the SIS judgment on 2026-08-13 (>99% foremarket share; Kodak/Epic factors not required), reviving a ~$140M claim (~$420M trebled, ~$1/share) and strengthening the hospital class case, whose trial the supervisor dates to 2027-09-14 (not independently verified by me). Probability-weighted cost ~$4/share including behavioral remedies that could widen the remanufacturing channel.

bear.story: U.S. procedure growth slides toward ~10% as ACA attrition (HCA uninsured admissions +23%) and Medicaid work requirements from 2027 keep benign procedures deferred, bariatric keeps shrinking, the EUP hit lands at the top of the 1-3% range with remanufacturers adding pressure, China share keeps falling, Hugo wins general-surgery clearance and Ottava early IDN deals, the hospital class trial goes badly, and rates stay above 5%; FY2028 EPS ~$12 at ~24.5x.

base.story: Procedure growth ~12-13% with ACA comps lapping during 2027, da Vinci 5 trade-ins (144 in Q2 vs 83) and ASC Xi sustain capital, EUP costs ~2% of I&A per procedure, competitors remain sub-scale through 2027, litigation an overhang not a loss; FY2028 EPS ~$13.45 at ~32x less ~$4 litigation.

bull.story: Deferred benign procedures return, OUS growth ~19-20% persists, EUP drives incremental volume as in 2020-21, Ottava and Hugo prove slow, rates ease from 5%; multiple re-rates toward ~40x on ~$14 EPS.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$300 the stock would trade at ~22x my FY2028 EPS ($13.45) and ~25x consensus FY2027 EPS, which only makes sense if procedure growth is structurally heading to single digits, competitors are taking meaningful U.S. soft-tissue share (Ottava multi-system IDN wins, Hugo winning general surgery after clearance), or instrument pricing erodes well beyond the Extended Use Program (e.g. an adverse class verdict forcing open the remanufacturing channel). Rates above 5% explain perhaps one or two turns of de-rating, not eleven; the 52-week low of $328.57 was set on sentiment after the Q2 guide, so a sustained break of ~$300 would signal a fundamental change rather than volatility.

reasoning: Round 2 revision after the supervisor's review, with ~9 follow-up searches/fetches. (1) I verified the HCA Q2 2026 10-Q directly on sec.gov: same-facility uninsured admissions +23.4% (consolidated +23.3%), outpatient surgeries -4.4% consolidated / -3.4% same-facility, inpatient -2.3%. My round-1 'correction' to +15% was wrong (the -4.4% was the consolidated figure), so the customer-side ACA headwind is larger than I weighted; with Medicaid work requirements from 2027-01-01 I raised the ACA drag on FY2027 EPS from ~1% to ~1.5%. (2) I accept that the 2020 EUP '-7% modeled, -2% actual' precedent is one secondary original on a COVID-distorted base, and now use a 1-3% I&A/procedure range (midpoint 2%); I add that third-party remanufacturing (Restore Robotics Xi clearances, allowed under Intuitive's contracts) is a second source of instrument price pressure in the same procedures. Net FY2027 EPS $12.00 -> $11.85, FY2028 $13.70 -> $13.45. (3) Macro: confirmed the Fed hike to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and the 10-year above 5% (~5.2% by Sept 26, highest since 2007); I cut the multiple from 33x to 32x and raised the FCF yield from 3.0% to 3.1%. I stop at 32x rather than 31x because my lane's competitive evidence still shows Ottava and Hugo sub-scale through 2027. (4) Litigation: confirmed the Ninth Circuit reversal (25-1372, 2026-08-13); I deduct ~$4/share expected cost. (5) Hugo general-surgery clearance: Medtronic gives no dated timeline, so it moves from an October event to undated headline risk. Fair value $452 -> $425. Scenarios bear $295 (28%) / base $425 (50%) / bull $560 (22%), mean ~$427 including spread. The ladder is a mixture of lognormals (sigmas 0.23/0.18/0.21), log-spread ~0.31 against 37% realized vol; median ~$415, P(>=401)=0.546 (from 0.604). One-month ladder is near-symmetric around $400.5 with an 11.5% sigma for the Oct 20 print. Sell-side average PT (~$476-509 depending on aggregator) is evidence that the market's analysts are above me, not the answer.
